# small_mechanisms: mechanism model and physical review

**Status: simulation acceptance, not validated sim-to-real.** The source identifies a Fellow-like kettle, an unresolved Cuckoo rice cooker and a capsule coffee machine, now visually identified by the separate calibration job as a Vertuo Creatista BVE850. There are no measured component weights, force traces, material tests or confirmed product identifiers. The requested portafilter bayonet is a hypothetical extension: the photographed machine has a hinged capsule head and the source notes explicitly question the identification of the handled accessory. It would be misleading to certify these mechanisms as the real appliances. The supplied geometry and metric registration are retained; no scale correction is invented.

## Deliverables and use

`mjcf/kettle.xml`, `mjcf/rice_cooker.xml`, and `mjcf/espresso_machine.xml` are individually loadable MuJoCo 3.5 models. `mjcf/small_mechanisms.xml` is their standalone side-by-side inspection scene. All OBJ dependencies are copied into relative `mjcf/meshes/`. Each object retains its source bottom-centre frame, +Z up, metres, kilograms, seconds, radians, newtons. The combined scene places objects at X = −0.38, 0, +0.39 m for inspection, **not the measured kitchen placement**. Every named engine element is prefixed `small_mechanisms_`, with the explicitly requested keyframe exception `rest`.

Initialize and advance with:

```python
import mujoco
from controller import MechanismController
m = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path('mjcf/small_mechanisms.xml')
d = mujoco.MjData(m)
mujoco.mj_resetDataKeyframe(m, d, m.key('rest').id)
mujoco.mj_forward(m, d)
c = MechanismController(m)
# Every physics substep, after applying external forces:
c.update(d)
mujoco.mj_step(m, d)
```

MJCF alone compiles and settles; its mechanical latches stay engaged unless the application uses the controller. There is no global MuJoCo callback. Controller state is held in each `MjData.eq_active`, so independent environments do not share latch state. A reset to `rest` resets controls and equalities. Both adhesion controls equal **1** in the rest keyframe. The controller sets the rice adhesion control to zero on release. The kettle adhesion control stays at 1: absence of contact makes its generalized force zero.

The builder uses `source_snapshot/` with SHA-256 provenance so concurrent upstream asset edits do not change this validated version. The shared rice-cooker asset was being regenerated during the final pass and its collision filenames changed; the snapshot preserves the already reviewed geometry. Updating to a newer upstream asset requires a deliberate rebase and another dynamics run.

Regenerate with `python build.py` from this folder in the supplied MuJoCo environment. `extract_materials.py` runs in Blender and recovers source Blender material colours, roughness and metal appearance absent from OBJ exports. `python tests/test_mechanisms.py` runs the complete acceptance suite and writes `tests/results.json` plus `evaluation/traces.json`. `MUJOCO_GL=egl python render_review.py` creates native MuJoCo inspection renders. `python make_plots.py` requires Matplotlib and Pillow and creates `review.jpg` and standalone PNG/PDF plots. No image-generation tool was used.

The explicit requested delivery directory takes precedence over the generic `scenes/test_scene_N` storage convention. This work makes no new scene capture or reconstruction, changes no website, and does not publish assets. Existing frame/pose replay under the layout job remains separate. Review images show **kinematic inspection poses**; the plots show **force-driven offline simulation**. No synchronized reconstruction video, new camera trajectory, online estimator or real-time claim is created by this mechanism job.

## Dimensional evidence and product checks

| Object | Retained visual dimensions, m | Evidence and limitations |
|---|---|---|
| Kettle | 0.210 × 0.277 × 0.2073 complete assembly | Source OBJ fit; vessel diameter 0.158, vessel height 0.178. Source notes distinguish handle/spout envelope from body box. Layout estimates vessel 0.230 × 0.250 × 0.245 and base 0.130 × 0.215 × 0.035, a substantial disagreement. |
| Rice cooker | 0.310 × 0.3224 × 0.3153 | Source OBJ, layout shell 0.310 × 0.320 × 0.310; rear hinge and button travel are inferred. Layout placement uncertainty is approximately 5–12 cm in source notes. |
| Coffee machine | 0.2795 × 0.2555 × 0.3985 source envelope | Source reconstruction box 0.270 × 0.241 × 0.390; scene layout box 0.400 × 0.320 × 0.365 includes different silhouette assumptions. Proposed filter installation changes its pose. |

An independent re-run of `ktools point` on f2484 at (412,683) and (725,685) returned WORLD [−0.811355, −1.241318, 1.170134] and [−0.931608, −1.038826, 1.170260] m. Their separation is **0.235508 m**, not a directly measured full cooker width. These are visible surface samples with perspective/occlusion and no known corresponding edge definition. They cannot justify silently shrinking the 0.31 m asset. Raw inputs, outputs and scale status are in `evaluation/measurements.json`. The articulation file was checked; it contains no measured kettle/cooker/coffee joint to use in place of the inferred mechanisms.

Published specifications are **comparators**, not confirmed identities:

* [Fellow manufacturer's Stagg EKG manual](https://ep-shopify.s3.amazonaws.com/related-documents/fellow/ekg/stagg-ekg-manual.pdf): 1.217 kg including base, nominal 0.9 L model. Its printed mixed-unit dimensions contain an inconsistent width conversion; do not derive calibration from that width. [Fellow base dimensions](https://help.fellowproducts.com/hc/en-us/articles/49490350679579-What-are-the-base-dimensions-of-Fellow-EKG-kettles) gives roughly 171 × 172 mm, about 25.4 mm high. The source asset's flatter, wider base does not match that reference, so its identity/scale remains unresolved.
* [Cuckoo CR-0675F product specifications](https://cuckooamerica.com/products/cr-0675f): 12.8 × 9.4 × 8.5 in = 325.1 × 238.8 × 215.9 mm; 10 lb = 4.536 kg. This is visibly a different control arrangement. Its weight does not establish the captured cooker's mass.
* The separate scale-calibration job visually identifies the photographed coffee machine as **Vertuo Creatista BVE850**, not Maestria. [Breville BVE850 specifications](https://www.breville.com/en-us/product/bve850) give 8.98 × 16.41 × 12.64 in (228.1 × 416.8 × 321.1 mm). [Manufacturer user manual](https://assets.breville.com/BVE850/BVE850_USCM_IB_120V_B23_FA.pdf) and [Nespresso assistance](https://www.nespresso.com/us/en/machine-assistance/vertuo-creatista) specify **8.7 kg**. The source mesh remains substantially taller and shallower than this product: a uniform scale alone cannot resolve that shape discrepancy. The simulated machine uses 8.7 kg plus the separate hypothetical 0.52 kg filter. Component allocation remains assumed. The serial label has not been read.
* [Nespresso Maestria manufacturer specifications](https://www.nespresso.com/us/en/order/machines/original/nespresso-maestria-aluminum): 5.3 kg; 170 × 385 × 302 mm; removable 1.4 L tank. This is another capsule machine with steam wand, **not an identification** of the source appliance, and does not establish a bayonet interface.

## Mass and inertia

All appliances are dry and empty. Liquid, rice, steam, thermal effects, pressure and cable loads are excluded. The kettle base, cooker housing and coffee chassis are fixed test fixtures; masses/inertias are still recorded, but fixture reaction prevents appliance sliding/tipping. Release these roots in a full scene if whole-appliance manipulation is required; the reported force thresholds then need re-evaluation.

| Body | Mass, kg | Justification |
|---|---:|---|
| Kettle vessel including handle/spout | 0.777 | Residual allocation from 1.217 kg comparator after base/dial/lid allocation; not weighed. |
| Kettle base | 0.350 | Source estimate for polymer base/electronics. |
| Kettle dial | 0.020 | Small metal/plastic knob prior, separate from base. |
| Kettle lid | 0.070 | Source estimate for thin lid and knob. |
| Cooker fixed housing/heater/liner | 2.528 | 79% of retained 3.2 kg source prior. |
| Cooker lid including vent | 0.656 | 20.5% of source total; uncertain hidden construction. |
| Cooker button | 0.016 | 0.5% of source total. |
| Coffee fixed assembly | 7.880 | Residual of manufacturer 8.7 kg machine mass after 0.4 kg tray, 0.3 kg tank and 0.12 kg wand priors; includes closed head/linkage/lever. Conditional on the visual BVE850 identification. |
| Coffee tray and cup support | 0.400 | Steel/plastic removable tray prior. |
| Empty water tank including top | 0.300 | Thin polymer reservoir prior. |
| Steam wand | 0.120 | Thin steel tube and grip prior. |
| Portafilter approximation | 0.520 | Generic metal basket and handle prior, not an observed product weight. |
| Bayonet mathematical carrier | 0.000001 | Numerical hinge carrier, not a physical extra part; fixed inertia 1e−9 kg m² per axis. |
| Rice striker child | 0 | Rigid child of lid; striker mass included in lid total. |

MuJoCo computes principal inertias and centres of mass from **collision geometry**, not render meshes: `inertiagrouprange="3 3"`. Explicit geom masses, primitive solid moments and convex mesh volume moments are combined by the parallel-axis theorem. This is a geometry-based composite approximation; it does not recover the hidden motor/heater mass distribution. Visual geoms have zero mass and no contacts. The generated table below lists every compiled body COM, inertia and inertia-frame quaternion.

Mass distributions: kettle vessel 70% tapered wall sectors, 18% annular floor, 12% equally across five handle/spout hulls; cooker housing 65% equally across eight wall hulls and 35% base; cooker lid all on lid hull; coffee chassis equally across four support boxes; tray 60% floor and 10% each of four rim strips; tank 20% bottom and 20% each wall; wand equally across five capsule segments; filter 55% annular basket, 25% floor, 20% handle. These allocations are assumptions and cannot establish accurate COMs from product weight alone.

## Joint and contact laws

All values below are engineering priors selected for plausible manipulation and then tested. **None of these efforts or dissipation values is hardware-measured.** Static joint friction has units N m for hinges and N for sliders; damping has units N m s/rad or N s/m; hinge armature is kg m² and slider armature kg. No powered position servo is used.

| Joint | Static friction | Damping | Armature | Spring / range and rationale |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Kettle dial | 0.001 | 0.0003 | 0.000002 | Continuous, no stops; 24 sinusoidal detents/revolution with 0.008 N m peak. At 10 mm radius, detent peak alone is 0.8 N fingertip force. Detents are requested, not observed. |
| Rice lid | 0.025 | 0.24 | 0.00015 | 2 N m/rad spring; unloaded spring reference 1.06 rad; 0…1.6 rad stops. Gravity, lid COM and friction yield about 45° after release. Spring at 0 supplies 2.12 N m before gravity/contact reactions. |
| Rice button | 0.4 | 10 | 0.002 | 1200 N/m soft spring, rest 0; travel 0…3 mm. Release at 2.2 mm: nominal slow push 0.4 + 1200×0.0022 = 3.04 N; force-step test brackets 3–4 N. High damping avoids spurious transient release. |
| Coffee tray | 1.8 | 3 | 0.01 | 0…120 mm; no return spring. Finger-pull friction prior; rail joint carries vertical load. Floor has 1 mm clearance above fixed support collider to avoid overconstraining the vertical rail support with a coincident friction plane. |
| Steam wand | 0.035 | 0.012 | 0.00002 | Vertical swivel −0.6…1.1 rad; no spring. Seal/bearing drag prior; no ball-joint tilt modeled. |
| Bayonet carrier | 0.18 | 0.035 | 0.00001 | 0…π/4 rad, rest π/4 locked; no return spring. 0.18 N m over a 64 mm grip arm predicts about 2.8 N tangential force. |
| Free vessel/lid/tank/filter | 0 joint drag | 0 | 0 | Unconstrained 6-DOF, contact-only resistance except the docked filter weld. No hidden slide restricting kettle/tank extraction. |

Dial torque is `−0.008 sin(24 q)` N m, implemented by the motor actuator before each substep. Its potential is `0.008/24 × (1−cos(24q))` J, so it is a passive detent law; its motor power must be included separately if auditing MuJoCo's built-in energy total. The dial test applies a force tangent to the *moving* knob, rather than a fixed world force that would reverse torque every half revolution.

Solver: 0.0005 s timestep, gravity 9.81 m/s², implicit-fast integration, Newton solver with 100 maximum iterations, tolerance 1e−10, elliptic contact cone and multicontact CCD. Normal contact `solref=(0.002,1)`; `solimp=(0.95,0.99,0.001)`. Generic limits use `solreflimit=(0.002,1)`, `solimplimit=(0.95,0.99,0.001)`. Cooker lid lower/upper stops and seal use the harder 0.001 s, critically damped response to limit reclosure impact penetration. Button stop uses 0.002 s. These are soft constraint time constants, not measured material moduli. Joint static-friction constraints use `solreffriction=(0.002,1)`, `solimpfriction=(0.999,0.9999,0.001)` to reduce artificial creep in low-inertia joints. Those solver settings are build defaults, including zeros/defaults for unspecified springs and friction.

Contact friction `(sliding, torsional, rolling) = (0.55, 0.005 m, 0.0001 m)` is a dry polymer/coating prior. Kettle gasket, rice gasket/striker and portafilter grip use sliding 0.8 for rubberlike contact; other two coefficients unchanged. No restitution coefficient is set: damping comes from the critically damped soft contact. These are uncertain surface priors, not texture-derived friction measurements.

### Latches and removability

**Kettle lid:** 2 N body adhesion acts only on the lid's one gasket collision mesh when it touches something. The empirical force-step breakaway includes its 0.6867 N weight, matching a predicted ~2.69 N vertical pull. This approximates a snug seal; no evidence establishes a real magnet. It can also attract an unrelated contacting surface after removal because MuJoCo adhesion targets a body rather than one named pair; a full task controller should disable it when the lid is away from the kettle if that behavior matters. The test verifies exactly zero generalized adhesion force out of contact while ctrl remains 1. Mesh-on-mesh lid contact replaces cylinder-on-thin-wedge contact that produced spurious deep contact results during tilt.

**Rice:** a rigid striker child isolates the 8 N adhesion actuator from other lid contacts. The striker at [0,−0.125,0.250] m meets a gasket at [0,−0.125,0.246] m. Both have half-sizes [0.016,0.008,0.002] m. An explicit pair uses 0.05 mm contact margin, zero gap: adhesion requires an active MuJoCo seal contact, with no long-range attraction. The margin is a small effective gasket skin, not an intentional geometric penetration. A joint equality models the unseen mechanical hook; it is not a finite-force magnetic breakaway. Hook failure under excessive handle pull is not modeled. A 4 N upward handle check verifies closed-state retention, while button force controls release.

The documented sensor rule is: release hook equality and seal adhesion when button travel reaches 2.2 mm; re-engage only when lid angle <0.012 rad, |lid speed| <0.08 rad/s and button travel <0.7 mm. Rule inputs are the same joint positions exposed by named joint-position sensors. Closure under an applied downward handle force is tested. No physical hook geometry was invented from absent evidence. Button collider is an outer thin pad offset 5 mm toward the front to leave the intended guide clearance, while the visual shank enters the housing. No contacts are suppressed to hide initial penetrations.

**Bayonet:** a fixed-bearing revolute carrier supplies the 45° travel and friction. The filter is a world free body welded to that carrier while docked, so applied handle forces drive the bearing. At angle <0.025 rad, the entry-slot sensor rule releases the weld. Reattachment is explicit `controller.dock(data)`: position within 1 mm, orientation within 0.01 rad and combined spatial speed norm <0.02 are required. This speed check is a conservative mixed-unit numerical guard, not a physical metric. The guard never teleports the object. The current software approximation omits actual lugs, ramps, pressure seal and axial locking preload. Those omissions are particularly important because the product itself is unverified. Equality solref is (0.003,1), solimp (0.99,0.999,0.001); no arbitrary force-threshold release is used.

## Collision geometry and fixed/moving separation

* Kettle: retained source handle and spout convex pieces; the solid vessel hull is replaced with 24 annular sectors in each of three tapered height bands, plus 24 floor sectors. Shell thickness 3 mm. Profile [z,r] = [0.019,0.077], [0.068,0.071], [0.139,0.047], [0.1843,0.043] m about [−0.009927,0.000841]. A 10 mm radius, 6 mm tall base post fits an 11 mm radius underside opening. This is locating contact, not a kinematic dock. The floor is 6 mm thick; lid gasket is a 48-sided convex disk. The source visual vessel still includes a shallow internal closure; collision access is open and probe-tested, but the visual interior is not a reconstructed liquid vessel. Spout lumen remains closed in collision, so pouring is unsupported.
* Cooker: original eight convex wall hulls and bottom preserve an open cavity; lid hull follows the rear hinge [0,0.158,0.248], axis [−1,0,0]. Button has independent slide along +Y. Hinge body and outer shell fixed; lid and vent one moving body. Interior liner is a generic completion, with no independently removable pot.
* Coffee: replace the original overlapping chassis/tank and solid tray/filter envelopes with four fixed support boxes, tray floor plus four rim boxes, tank bottom plus four wall boxes, five wand capsules and a 24-piece filter ring. Tank thickness 3 mm, basket radii 27/34 mm, basket nominal height 14 mm. Broad unseen chassis surfaces remain conservative support approximations; internal wiring and rails omitted. Source brew head and linkage are fixed closed for this requested mechanism test; their source visual animation is not validated here. Source tank lid is included visually with the tank, with no separate lid joint/collider. Tray grate holes are visual; floor supports objects below the visible grate. No hidden collision exclusions are used.

All generated mesh collision pieces are convex by construction; source convex meshes are checked separately in the automated geometry audit. Free-body masses and articulated masses never include render meshes. A 12 mm diameter, 10 g sphere subjected to an additional 0.1 N downward force checks usable kettle, cooker and tank collision cavities; this is not fluid validation.

## Scaling and integration

The separate `../../scale_calibration/calibration.json` became available during this work. It proposes **c = 0.9411280362**, with conditional approximate interval [0.8281726, 1.0539092], and explicitly labels local depth distortion unresolved. This delivery retains **PARAMS.scale = 1.0**, so its geometry stays in the supplied source-asset frame awaiting consistent scene-wide application. Do not multiply an already-corrected scene twice. The candidate is recorded in `evaluation/measurements.json`; it is not presented as an established ground-truth scale. At that candidate scale the source coffee height would still be 375 mm versus the 321 mm product reference, so geometry refitting remains necessary for verified real dimensions.

`params.py:PARAMS` is the editable parameter dictionary. All authored mechanism geometry, mesh scales, pivots, force-site arms, prismatic travel and removal thresholds derive from it. Source mesh coordinates are in their source OBJ files, and `scale` uniformly multiplies them at MJCF compile time. Inertias derived from geometry change as scale² at unchanged mass; product masses, spring rates, applied forces and torques stay independently specified. Thus changing metric scale does **not** promise unchanged spring opening angle or force thresholds: those must be rerun and, if needed, recalibrated. The combined layout offsets also scale. Render-only inspection camera/pose distances are illustrative.

`isaac/actuators.py` supplies an `ActuatorBaseCfg`/custom actuator, explicit passive spring/detent/damping laws, two-stage button stop, contact-gated seal torque and compliant hook approximation. Joint friction and armature values match the table. Damping is applied once in the custom effort kernel, with simulator actuator damping set to zero. Isaac Sim 5.0+ uses force/torque joint-friction units; older dimensionless PhysX friction is not equivalent. [Isaac Lab actuator documentation](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/main/source/api/lab/isaaclab.actuators.html) and [joint friction version notes](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/develop/docs/source/concepts/actuators.rst) describe those interfaces. The environment must provide actual striker contact reports and enable/disable the USD latch joint; this adapter alone does not build the USD scene or detachable objects. Kettle contact adhesion must likewise be applied through rigid-body contact handling, not an always-on joint torque. Only the Torch laws were run here; full Isaac/PhysX equivalence is **untested**.

[MuJoCo adhesion reference](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.5.0/XMLreference.html#actuator-adhesion) documents body-targeted, contact-dependent adhesion with gain in N. That implementation detail is why the rice striker is its own child body.

## Acceptance interpretation and remaining physical work

Force tests write `xfrc_applied` with both the site force and `(site − COM) × force`; they do not set joint positions to create measured travel. The kettle lift force can tip the vessel before its full weight is supported, so the reported COM-rise threshold is **not** a pure vertical pull-off weight measurement. Bayonet force is sampled at the moving handle. Breakaway values are brackets from independent reset/settle/force trials, not finely resolved material constants. Every integration substep checks finite state, MuJoCo warnings and contact depth ≤2 mm. Rest tests check every standalone model and the combined assembly. Passive spring-plus-gravity energy decay is tested after handle-force removal, apart from switching and actuator work. Render poses intentionally are not used as dynamics evidence.

To establish real-world agreement: confirm labels; weigh each removable part; independently measure overall sizes, hinge and grip positions; record at least five slow push/pull trials with a force gauge; measure lid release/opening time and unforced resting angle; repeat with relevant contents; measure contact friction on the actual countertop. Fit against those traces and use held-out repetitions for validation. In particular, do not use the hypothetical portafilter bayonet as a claim about the captured capsule machine. Missing hardware data is a material limit of this delivery.

The following generated sections list final results, exact compiled body inertias and the complete parameter dictionary. They are tied to the saved build and test run, not manually transcribed performance claims.

<!-- GENERATED REPORT -->

## Final run

MuJoCo 3.5.0; **14 tests, all passing**; 39.488 s actual test wall time on this host, including setup/compilation and Python assertions. This is not simulator throughput or reconstruction latency. Scale 1.0.

|---|---:|
| Kettle tipping/COM-rise threshold (not pure lift weight) | 6 N |
| Lid pull-off bracket | >2 to ≤3 N |
| Button release bracket | >3 to ≤4 N |
| Button travel at 5 N | 3.0189 mm |
| Passive lid equilibrium | 43.8886° |
| Lid full-open soft stop | 1.600009 rad |
| Tray breakaway bracket | >1.5 to ≤2 N |
| Tray full extension | 120.0027 mm |
| Bayonet breakaway bracket | >2 to ≤3 N |
| Tank >5 mm extraction after 150 ms | >3 to ≤4 N (weight is 2.943 N) |
| Rice reclosure | latched |
| Rice release energy decrease | 0.033609 J |

Worst recorded penetration across the reported trajectories: **1.5734 mm** (limit 2 mm). Initial depth is at numerical round-off (~1e−9 m). 137/137 collision mesh files are convex, watertight and positive-volume in `evaluation/collision_audit.json`; primitives are convex by definition. No NaN/Inf or MuJoCo warning occurred. The three Isaac tests cover Torch laws only.

Twelve native inspection renders took 4.030 s wall time, excluding authorship, material extraction and plot composition.

## Exact editable parameter ledger

Geometry coordinates and half-extents are source-frame metres before `scale`; imported OBJ vertices are the other source of shape coordinates. Masses and effort settings are SI. `view` is rendering only; `test` defines acceptance/probe settings; `isaac` defines adapter-only compliant stop/hook priors. Each geometry parameter is an inferred collision completion tied to the source bounds, rather than an independent measurement. All unknowns and source-based allocations are identified above.

```json
{
  "scale": 1.0,
  "timestep": 0.0005,
  "gravity": 9.81,
  "contact": {
    "friction": [
      0.55,
      0.005,
      0.0001
    ],
```
